Some names describe features: Rithmah, “broom bush”; Rimmon Perez, “pomegranate of the breach”; Libnah, “white”; Haradah, “trembling”; Makheloth, “assemblies”; Moseroth, “bonds”; Bene Jaakan, “sons of Jaakan”; Jotbathah, “pleasantness”; Ezion Geber, perhaps “backbone of a man,” at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba.

The fifth month, Av. Because the months followed the moon, the date falls in different parts of July and August from year to year. This is the only place in the Bible that gives the date of Aaron’s death.
Iyim, “ruins,” is a short form of Iye Abarim (verse 44).
Beth Jeshimoth means “house of the wastes.” Abel Shittim means “meadow of acacias”; compare Shittim in 25:1.
Or “figured stones,” carved images used in worship.

verses.text: Yahweh said to Moses,
“Tell the Israelites: The country you are about to enter, Canaan, will fall to you as your inheritance. Its edges are as follows.
Your southern side will start at the Desert of Zin along the edge of Edom. Your southern border begins at the eastern end of the Dead Sea.{a}
From there it bends south of Scorpion Pass,{b} crosses to Zin, and finishes south of Kadesh Barnea. Next it reaches Hazar Addar, then moves along to Azmon,
where it turns toward the Brook of Egypt{c} and ends at the Mediterranean Sea.
“Your western border is the coast of the Great Sea.{d} That is your border on the west.
“Your northern edge will be drawn from the Great Sea across to Mount Hor.{e}
From Mount Hor, trace it to Lebo Hamath, and the boundary finishes at Zedad.
Then it goes on to Ziphron and stops at Hazar Enan. That makes up your northern boundary.
“On the east, run your boundary from Hazar Enan down to Shepham.
The border runs down from Shepham to Riblah, east of Ain, and continues down to the hills on the east side of the Sea of Galilee.{f}
It then follows the Jordan down and ends at the Dead Sea. Those are the borders enclosing your land.”
Moses told the Israelites, “You will receive this land by lot. Yahweh has decided that it belongs to nine and a half tribes.
Reuben’s tribe, Gad’s tribe, and half of Manasseh’s tribe have already received their inheritance, clan by clan.
Those two and a half tribes were given land on the Jordan’s east side, across from Jericho, toward the rising sun.”
Yahweh told Moses,
“The men who will assign the land among you are Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
Pick a leader from each tribe to take part in dividing the inheritance.
Their names are these. For Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
from Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
for Dan, Bukki son of Jogli, a leader;
for Joseph’s descendants, Hanniel son of Ephod, a leader from Manasseh,
and the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan for Ephraim;
from Zebulun, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach;
from Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan;
from Asher, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi;
and from Naphtali, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud.{g}
These are the men Yahweh appointed to divide the land of Canaan among the Israelites.”

notes.text: Hebrew “Salt Sea,” the Dead Sea.
Akrabbim means “scorpions.”
Probably the Wadi el-Arish in northern Sinai.
Hebrew “the Great Sea,” the Mediterranean.
Not the Mount Hor of 20:22, but a mountain in the north, probably in the Lebanon range.
Hebrew “Sea of Chinnereth,” which may mean “harp-shaped.” This is the Sea of Galilee.

Several of these names include a name for God: Shemuel, “name of God”; Elidad, “God has loved”; Hanniel, “grace of God”; Kemuel, perhaps “assembly of God”; Elizaphan, “God has protected”; Paltiel, “God is my deliverance”; Pedahel, “God has redeemed.” Bukki perhaps means “proved”; Ahihud, “my brother is majesty.”

subheads.16: The men who will divide the land

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, near Jericho, and said,
“Instruct the Israelites to set aside towns for the Levites from the land they inherit, and to add open grazing land around each town.
The towns will be where they live, and the pastures will be for their cattle, their herds, and all their other animals.
The pastures around the towns you give the Levites will reach outward 1,500 feet{a} from the town wall in every direction.

Measure 3,000 feet{b} out from the town on the east, 3,000 feet on the south, 3,000 feet on the west, and 3,000 feet on the north, with the town in the center. This will be the grazing land for their towns.
“Of the towns you give the Levites, six are to be cities of refuge, where someone who has killed a person can run to be safe. Besides these, give forty-two more towns.
In all, you will give the Levites forty-eight towns, each with its pastureland.
The towns come out of the land held by the Israelites. Take more from the large tribes and fewer from the small ones. Each tribe gives towns to the Levites in proportion to the land it receives.”
Yahweh said to Moses,
“Speak to the Israelites: After you cross the Jordan into Canaan,
choose cities to serve as cities of refuge, where a person who kills someone accidentally can run to.
These cities will shield him from the one who avenges the dead,{c} so the killer is not executed until he has had a hearing before the community.
Six cities of refuge will be yours to give.
Three will be east of the Jordan, and three in Canaan itself.
These six cities are a refuge for Israelites, and also for foreigners and outsiders living among them, so that anyone who kills a person by accident can run there.
“If a man strikes someone with an iron tool and the victim dies, he is a murderer, and he must be executed.
If he strikes with a rock held in his hand that is large enough to kill, and the man dies, he is a murderer, and he must be executed.
The same goes for a wooden club big enough to kill: if the man dies, the attacker is a murderer and must be executed.
The one who avenges the dead is to execute the murderer. When he finds him, he is to put him to death.
If someone shoves a person out of hatred, or throws something at him while lying in wait, and the person dies,
or if out of hostility someone strikes another with his fist and he dies, the attacker must be put to death. He is a murderer, and the avenger of the dead is to kill him when he finds him.
“But suppose someone shoves a person without any hostility, or throws something at him without lying in wait,
or drops a stone big enough to kill on someone he did not see, and the person dies. If he was not the person’s enemy and meant him no harm,
then the community is to judge between the attacker and the avenger according to these rules.
The community will rescue the killer from the avenger and return him to the city of refuge where he fled. There he stays until the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil, dies.
Should the killer ever step beyond the border of the city of refuge he ran to,
and the avenger finds him there and kills him, the avenger is not guilty of murder.
The killer has to stay in his city of refuge until the high priest dies. Only after that may he return to his own property.
These are to be rules of law for you in every generation, wherever you live.
“Anyone who kills a person is to be executed as a murderer, but only when witnesses testify. A single witness is not enough to condemn anyone to death.
Never accept a payment to spare the life of a murderer who deserves to die. He must be put to death.
Also never accept a payment from someone who ran to a city of refuge, to let him go home to his land before the high priest dies.
Never pollute the land you live in. Blood pollutes the land, and the only way to make things right for the land after blood has been shed on it is by the blood of the one who shed it.
Keep the land where you live clean, since I live in it. I, Yahweh, live among the Israelites.”

notes.text: Hebrew “a thousand cubits,” about 450 meters. A cubit was about 18 inches (45 centimeters).
Hebrew “two thousand cubits,” about 900 meters. How verses 4 and 5 fit together is uncertain. Verse 5 may give the length of each side of a square around the town.
Hebrew go’el, the nearest relative, responsible for avenging a killing. See the note at 5:8.

verses.text: The family heads of the clan of Gilead, descendants of Machir son of Manasseh and of the families of Joseph, came forward and spoke in front of Moses and the leaders, who were the family heads of Israel.
They said, “Yahweh ordered my lord to divide the land among the Israelites by lot. My lord was also ordered by Yahweh to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

But suppose they marry men from another Israelite tribe. Their land would be taken from our ancestors’ inheritance and added to the tribe they marry into. It would be taken away from the share assigned to us.
And when the Israelites hold their Jubilee,{a} the land of those women would be added to the tribe they married into, and it would be lost from the inheritance of our ancestors’ tribe.”
So Moses gave the Israelites this order from Yahweh: “What the tribe of Joseph’s descendants say is right.
Yahweh’s command for Zelophehad’s daughters is this: Let them marry whoever pleases them, provided the husband belongs to a clan of their father’s tribe.
Israelite land must never move from tribe to tribe. Each Israelite is to keep the inheritance of his ancestors’ tribe.
Any daughter in an Israelite tribe who comes into land must take a husband from her father’s tribe, so that every Israelite family keeps its ancestral land.
Land cannot go from one tribe to another. Each of the Israelite tribes will keep its own inheritance.”
Zelophehad’s daughters did as Yahweh commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, Zelophehad’s five daughters, married their cousins on the father’s side.
Their husbands came from the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph, so their property stayed in the tribe and clan of their father.
These are the commands and rules Yahweh gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.

notes.text: The Jubilee was the fiftieth year, when land returned to its original family owners (Leviticus 25:8-17).
